newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rare Rembrandt copperplate put on show in Berlin.
newsitem.headline: Rare Rembrandt copperplate put on show in Berlin.

text.p: British-based auctioneers and art specialists Christie's on Friday put on show a rare Rembrandt copperplate that was discovered recently attached to the back of a painting after being lost for centuries.
Christie's said it had bought the painting in London from a man whose family had paid 60 pounds ($100 at current exchange rates) for it in 1946 in a shop in the northern English county of Yorkshire.
They had no idea the valuable 17th century copperplate, titled "Abraham Entertaining the Angels", was attached.
Art historians say the plate, one of only 82 in the world, is worth up to 45,000 pounds because of its pristine condition. Christie's plans to auction it in London on June 26.

"None of the other 81 plates by Rembrandt were used for an oil painting," said Christie's print specialist Liesbeth Heenk. "It is a very, very rare work of art, a profoundly exciting discovery." ($ = 0.609 British Pounds)
